name: Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency
description: Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency (Fèi Shèn Yáng Xū, 肺肾阳虚) is a empty TCM pattern. Key signs: Chronic cough with copious thin clear sputum, Shortness of breath...

timing_worsening_explanation: Symptoms tend to be worst in the early morning (3-5 AM, when the Lung channel is most active on the organ clock) and in the pre-dawn hours (3-7 AM), with coughing and wheezing often disturbing sleep during these times. Winter and cold damp seasons bring significant worsening. Symptoms also flare during weather transitions, particularly when cold fronts arrive. The late afternoon and evening (5-7 PM, Kidney time on the organ clock) may bring increased lower back aching, fatigue, and nocturia. Patients often feel relatively better in the warmth of midday. Over the longer term, the pattern tends to worsen gradually year by year if untreated, particularly through repeated winter exacerbations.
practitioner_notes:
Diagnosing this pattern requires identifying signs of Yang deficiency in both the Lungs and the Kidneys simultaneously. The key diagnostic logic works as follows: the Lungs govern Qi and respiration in the upper body, while the Kidneys 'grasp' or anchor Qi in the lower body. When Kidney Yang fails, it can no longer provide the foundational warmth that supports all other organs, including the Lungs. When Lung Yang (or Lung Qi with cold signs) also weakens, the Lungs cannot properly descend and distribute fluids or manage respiration. The result is a combined upper-and-lower deficiency cold pattern.
Practitioners look for the hallmark combination of respiratory symptoms (chronic cough or wheezing with thin watery sputum, shortness of breath worsened by exertion) alongside Kidney Yang deficiency signs (cold limbs and back, sore weak lower back and knees, frequent or copious clear urination, and possibly urinary incontinence when coughing). The tongue and pulse provide critical confirmation: a pale, puffy tongue with white slippery coating and a deep, slow, weak pulse (especially weak in both the Lung and Kidney positions) strongly support this diagnosis.
It is important to distinguish this from Lung-Kidney Qi Deficiency, which shares the breathlessness and fatigue but lacks prominent cold signs. It also differs from Spleen-Kidney Yang Deficiency, where digestive symptoms (pre-dawn diarrhoea, abdominal cold) are more prominent than respiratory ones. The pattern is commonly seen in chronic lung disease that has progressed over years to affect the Kidneys, or in elderly patients with constitutional decline.
pathophysiology: The Kidney's warming fire is too weak to support the Lungs, so both organs fail to properly manage breathing, fluid transformation and the body's defence against cold.
treatment_principle: Warm and tonify the Yang of the Lungs and Kidneys, assist Qi reception and transform fluids
typical_timeline: 3-6 months minimum for noticeable improvement, 6-12 months or longer for chronic or severe cases. Seasonal treatment intensification during autumn and winter (when cold challenges the body most) is advisable.
formula_modifications:
If there is noticeable fluid retention or oedema in the legsAdd Fu Ling (Poria), Ze Xie (Alisma), and Che Qian Zi (Plantago seed) to promote water metabolism. The weakened Kidney Yang is unable to properly transform and move fluids, so these herbs support the draining of accumulated water without further depleting the body.
If wheezing and breathlessness are the dominant symptomsAdd Ge Jie (Gecko), Zi Su Zi (Perilla seed), and increase the dosage of Bu Gu Zhi. These strengthen the Kidney's ability to grasp the breath and help the Lung descend Qi. Ge Jie is especially powerful for anchoring breathing in severe cases.
If the person also feels very tired and has poor appetiteAdd Huang Qi (Astragalus), Dang Shen (Codonopsis), and Bai Zhu (Atractylodes). These herbs strengthen the Spleen and raise Qi. When Kidney Yang is depleted, the Spleen (the digestive system) often weakens too because the Kidney fire that normally supports digestion is insufficient. Strengthening the Spleen ensures that nutrients from food can actually reach and replenish the Lungs and Kidneys.
If there is copious thin watery sputumAdd Gan Jiang (dried ginger) and Xi Xin (Asarum) to warm the Lungs and dissolve cold phlegm. This combination specifically targets cold fluids that have accumulated in the Lung because Yang is too weak to transform them.
If there is significant lower back pain and cold kneesAdd Du Zhong (Eucommia bark), Xu Duan (Dipsacus), and Niu Xi (Achyranthes) to strengthen the lower back, bones and sinews. The Kidney governs the bones and lower back, and when its Yang is depleted, these structures lose their warming support and become painful and weak.

causes_details: [{"cause_title": "Chronic respiratory illness damaging both Lung and Kidney", "explanation": "Long-standing lung conditions like chronic cough, asthma, or recurrent bronchitis gradually deplete the Lung's Qi. In TCM, the Lungs and Kidneys have a special relationship: the Lungs send Qi downward, and the Kidneys 'grasp' and anchor it to support deep breathing. When Lung Qi has been weak for a long time, the Kidneys must work harder to compensate. Eventually, this extra burden drains the Kidney's warming power (Yang), and both organs become deficient together. This is a classic example of the principle that prolonged illness of any organ eventually reaches the Kidneys, because the Kidneys are the deepest reservoir of the body's vital resources."}, {"cause_title": "Ageing and natural decline of Kidney Yang", "explanation": "As people age, their Kidney Essence and Yang naturally decline. The Kidney Yang is considered the root of all Yang in the body, providing warmth and motive force to every other organ. When this root fire weakens with age, the Lungs are among the first organs affected because they sit in the upper body and depend on the Kidney's warmth rising upward to keep them functioning well. This is why elderly people commonly develop shortness of breath, chronic cough with thin watery sputum, and cold intolerance, signs that both Lung and Kidney Yang are waning together."}, {"cause_title": "Excessive exposure to cold and damp environments", "explanation": "Prolonged exposure to cold weather, cold and damp working conditions, or habitually consuming cold and raw foods can directly injure the body's Yang. Cold is a Yin pathogen that contracts and slows things down. It first attacks the Lung (the most superficial organ) and, if it persists, penetrates deeper to damage Kidney Yang. When both organs lose their warmth, the body cannot properly warm itself, transform fluids, or maintain normal breathing."}, {"cause_title": "Overwork, exhaustion and excessive sexual activity", "explanation": "The Kidneys store Essence, which is the material basis for both Kidney Yin and Kidney Yang. Chronic overwork, physical exhaustion, and excessive sexual activity all draw heavily on Kidney Essence. As Essence declines, Kidney Yang weakens because there is less fuel to sustain the body's warming fire. Once Kidney Yang is compromised, it can no longer support the Lung, leading to progressive respiratory weakness and the combined Lung-Kidney Yang Deficiency pattern."}, {"cause_title": "Improper treatment with excessively cold or bitter herbs", "explanation": "In TCM, bitter and cold herbs (used to clear heat) can damage Yang if used inappropriately or for too long. If someone with an underlying Yang-deficient constitution is treated with strong cooling medicines, this can extinguish the body's warming fire. The Lung and Kidney, being particularly vulnerable to cold, may both become Yang-depleted. This is a reminder of the classical principle that treatment must always be tailored to the individual's constitution."}]

formulas.name: You Gui Wan
formulas.description: A stronger Yang-warming formula for more severe Kidney Yang depletion with Essence and Blood deficiency. It uses pure tonification without any draining herbs, making it suitable for pronounced cold signs, exhaustion and weakened constitution.

formulas.name: Ren Shen Lu Rong Tang
formulas.description: Specifically targets the Lung-Kidney axis by combining Ginseng (to tonify Lung Qi) with walnut (to warm Kidney Yang and help it grasp Qi). Directly addresses wheezing and dyspnoea from the Kidney failing to anchor the breath.

formulas.name: Bu Fei Tang
formulas.description: Tonifies Lung Qi and addresses the Lung component of this pattern. Often used as a base when Lung Qi deficiency is more prominent, with additions for Kidney Yang warming.

formulas.name: Gu Ben Ke Chuan Pian
formulas.description: A prepared formula used for the remission phase of chronic asthma and COPD with Lung-Kidney deficiency. It stabilises the root by warming the Kidneys and consolidating the Lungs.

herbs.name: Lai Fu Zi
herbs.description: The primary herb for restoring Kidney Yang. Fu Zi (Aconite root, prepared) is hot, acrid and sweet, and powerfully warms the Mingmen fire. It drives cold from the interior and rescues depleted Yang. Always used in its processed form to reduce toxicity.

herbs.name: Rou Gui
herbs.description: Cinnamon bark warms the Kidney Yang and mingmen fire, and assists Fu Zi in restoring the root warming function. It also warms the channels and promotes the movement of Qi and Blood.

herbs.name: Bu Gu Zhi
herbs.description: Psoralea fruit warms Kidney Yang and specifically helps the Kidney grasp Qi from the Lungs. It is a key herb for treating wheezing and dyspnoea caused by the Kidney's failure to anchor breathing.

herbs.name: Hu Tao Ren
herbs.description: Walnut meat warms the Lungs and Kidneys simultaneously. It helps the Kidney grasp Lung Qi and also warms the Lungs to relieve chronic cough and wheezing from cold deficiency.

herbs.name: Ge Jie
herbs.description: Gecko tonifies both Lung and Kidney Yang, strengthening the Kidney's ability to receive Qi and the Lung's ability to descend it. Particularly useful for severe chronic wheezing with pronounced Yang deficiency.

herbs.name: Dong Chong Xia Cao
herbs.description: Cordyceps simultaneously tonifies Lung Yin and Kidney Yang, making it ideal for cases where there is deficiency in both organs without excessive heat or cold. It supports both breathing and the root vitality.

herbs.name: Zi He Che
herbs.description: Placenta hominis is a powerful substance that tonifies Qi, Blood, and Essence and warms the Kidney Yang. It helps restore severely depleted constitutional resources in chronic exhaustion.

herbs.name: Yin Yang Huo
herbs.description: Epimedium warms Kidney Yang and strengthens the sinews and bones. It helps address the cold limbs, soreness and weakness in the lower back and knees that characterise this pattern.

herbs.name: Wu Wei Zi
herbs.description: Schisandra fruit astringes Lung Qi and contains Kidney Essence. It prevents the leakage of Qi and fluids and helps anchor breathing, useful as a supporting herb in this pattern.

acupoints.name: Feishu BL-13
acupoints.description: The Back-Shu point of the Lung. Directly tonifies and warms Lung Qi when combined with moxibustion. It strengthens the Lung's descending and dispersing functions.

acupoints.name: Shenshu BL-23
acupoints.description: The Back-Shu point of the Kidney. A primary point for all Kidney deficiency patterns. With moxibustion, it powerfully warms Kidney Yang and strengthens the lower back.

acupoints.name: Mingmen DU-4
acupoints.description: Located on the Du Mai between the Kidneys, this point directly warms and tonifies the 'Gate of Vitality' (mingmen fire). Moxibustion here is essential for restoring the root Yang of the body.

acupoints.name: Guanyuan REN-4
acupoints.description: On the Ren Mai below the navel, this point tonifies original Qi and warms the lower Jiao. It helps restore the Kidney's foundational warming and grasping functions.

acupoints.name: Taixi KI-3
acupoints.description: The Source point of the Kidney channel. Tonifies both Kidney Yin and Yang. Used here to strengthen the Kidney's root function and its ability to receive Qi from the Lungs.

acupoints.name: Taiyuan LU-9
acupoints.description: The Source point and Hui-meeting point of the vessels on the Lung channel. Tonifies Lung Qi and strengthens the Lung's role in governing Qi and respiration.

acupoints.name: Shanzhong REN-17
acupoints.description: The influential point for Qi, located on the chest. It regulates Qi in the upper Jiao, benefits breathing and supports the Lung's descending function.

acupoints.name: Zusanli ST-36
acupoints.description: The most important point for tonifying Qi and Blood overall. It supports the Spleen and Stomach (the post-natal root) to generate the resources needed to replenish both Lung and Kidney.

acupoints.name: Fuliu KI-7
acupoints.description: The Metal point on the Kidney channel. Tonifies Kidney Yang and has a specific action in regulating water metabolism, making it particularly useful when there is fluid retention.

faqs.question: What is Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency in TCM?
faqs.answer: The Kidney's warming fire is too weak to support the Lungs, so both organs fail to properly manage breathing, fluid transformation and the body's defence against cold.

faqs.question: What are the key signs of Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency?
faqs.answer: Key signs include: Chronic cough with copious thin clear sputum, Shortness of breath that worsens with physical activity, Wheezing or difficulty breathing, Feeling cold all over especially the back and limbs, Sore weak lower back and knees, Frequent urination especially at night, Fatigue and lack of stamina, Spontaneous sweating, Catching colds easily, Dizziness or light-headedness, Puffiness of the face and limbs, Low soft voice, No desire to speak.

faqs.question: What formulas treat Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency?
faqs.answer: Common formulas for Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency include: You Gui Wan, Ren Shen Lu Rong Tang, Bu Fei Tang, Gu Ben Ke Chuan Pian.

faqs.question: What Western conditions relate to Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency?
faqs.answer: This pattern is associated with: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), Chronic bronchitis, Emphysema, Chronic asthma (cold type), Pulmonary heart disease (cor pulmonale), Hypothyroidism, Chronic kidney disease, Adrenal insufficiency, Congestive heart failure (early stages), Chronic fatigue syndrome.

faqs.question: What is the treatment principle for Lung and Kidney Yang Deficiency?
faqs.answer: Warm and tonify the Yang of the Lungs and Kidneys, assist Qi reception and transform fluids
